where: crates/blaze-cargo/src/cli.rs:749 (`let mut out = io::stdout().lock()`, held for the whole command)
what: Writing a test executable's stdout on from another thread through `io::stdout()` would never return: the command's thread holds std's stdout lock for the whole command. Found by reading, before any run; the relay writes to a duplicate of the descriptor instead.
cost: would have been a hang of every piped `blaze test`; fifteen minutes
cause: a process-wide lock taken for a command's life, in one function, with nothing at the other writers to say so
fix: the command's stdout is passed to what writes it, not locked globally
